business.title: Divergent financing responses in lithium exploration: descriptive time-series evidence from fiscal and enterprise channels (2015-2024)
business.desc: Exploration investment in critical minerals is typically analysed as an aggregate process, leaving comparatively little evidence on how financing composition varies across institutional channels under changing commodity price conditions. Using annual data on lithium exploration during 2015–2024, this study disaggregates total exploration expenditure into central, provincial, and enterprise components and examines how their relative contributions are associated with two temporal representations of lithium price conditions. The results document distinct descriptive patterns across financing channels. Higher lagged lithium prices are associated with increased public exploration expenditure and a corresponding decline in the enterprise financing share, primarily because public appropriations increase more rapidly than enterprise-side spending. By contrast, annual lithium price increases are associated with a higher enterprise financing share. Component-level analysis further indicates that these descriptive patterns are consistent with differences in the evolution of public appropriations and enterprise-side spending over the study period. These findings document channel-specific differences in financing composition within an institutional setting characterized by multi-level planning and budgeting processes. Given the short annual time series and associated data limitations, the findings should be interpreted as suggestive descriptive empirical associations rather than as evidence of causal or generalizable behavioral relationships. By focusing on financing composition rather than aggregate expenditure, this study shows that analyses based solely on aggregate exploration expenditure do not fully capture differences across financing channels under changing price conditions. The findings are specific to a single national setting and the lithium exploration sector and should not be interpreted as generalizable beyond this national and sectoral context without further evidence.

business.title: Understanding the economic implications of Down syndrome: labour market and healthcare perspectives
business.desc: Down syndrome presents significant economic challenges for families navigating complex healthcare systems. This study explores the economic burden and healthcare accessibility for Saudi families managing Down syndrome care, emphasizing urban-rural disparities within the dual public-private healthcare system. Using a cross-sectional survey of 220 families from Riyadh and Al-Jouf regions, multiple regression and service integration analyses were conducted. Results indicate that monthly care costs consume approximately one-third of average household income, with medical expenses and daily care hours showing the strongest associations with total care cost, while higher government support was associated with lower reported care costs. Significant urban-rural gaps emerged in therapy access and educational support. Insurance coverage and specialized service access were notably higher in urban areas, while transportation costs disproportionately burdened rural families. These findings indicate scope for strengthened government support, improved rural healthcare infrastructure, and insurance reform. On this basis, the study sets out targeted policy options and the potential value of a centralized database for monitoring healthcare costs, with a view to informing evidence-based strategies aligned with Vision 2030 healthcare transformation goals.

business.title: Point-of-care hearing screening using consumer wireless earbuds in patients with USH2A-associated retinal disease: a prospective pilot feasibility study
business.desc: Usher syndrome type 2 (USH2) may be under-recognized in ophthalmology practice due to variable hearing loss severity and limited point-of-care audiometry. In this prospective pilot study at the Singapore National Eye Centre (November 2024 to February 2025) we evaluated a consumer earbud hearing test in patients with USH2A-associated retinal disease and explored cross-sectional relationships between hearing and visual measures. Thirteen patients with biallelic USH2A pathogenic variants (median age 45 years, range 29-81) and thirteen age- and sex-matched comparison participants underwent supervised air-conduction threshold estimation using AirPods Pro 2. All participants completed testing without failure, repetition or technical error. Among patients, median test duration was 4.5 minutes (range 3.6–5.1), and three required physical guidance. These feasibility outcomes are reported descriptively and post hoc. Right-ear pure-tone average (PTA4-R) ranged from 13.00 to 84.25 dB HL (median 48.25 dB HL) and ellipsoid zone (EZ) width ranged from 0 to 7,972 μm (median 1,037 μm). After adjustment for age, higher PTA4-R showed a negative association estimate with EZ width (β = −57.36 μm/dB, 95% CI −117.56 to 2.83; nominal p = 0.0597) and a positive association estimate with best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in logMAR units (β = 0.02793 logMAR/dB, 95% CI 0.00429 to 0.05156; nominal p = 0.0251). Neither met the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold (adjusted p = 0.1194 and 0.0501, respectively). Earbud-derived threshold configurations resembled previously described USH2A-associated patterns, but agreement with calibrated clinical audiometry was not assessed. Formal audiological evaluation remains necessary for diagnosis and management.
